rules.title: Ban the Box for Housing - Criminal History Inquiry Timing and Scope Restrictions
rules.quote: Inquiry into and consideration of any applicant's criminal history shall take place only after the applicant has submitted a formal application.
rules.summary: Landlords and real estate brokers may not inquire into an applicant's criminal history until after the applicant has submitted a formal application for housing.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to rental, lease, or sublease of real property, except single apartments in two-family dwellings where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in owner-occupied single-family dwellings.
rules.exemption_note: Exemptions for owner-occupied two-family dwellings (one unit rented) and rooms in owner-occupied single-family dwellings.
rules.penalty: First violation: fine up to $500. Each subsequent violation: fine up to $1,000.

rules.title: Ban the Box for Housing - Limits on Consideration of Criminal History
rules.quote: A landlord or real estate broker shall be permitted to inquire about: Indictable offense convictions in New Jersey (or, if from any other state or jurisdiction, convictions for conduct which, if committed in New Jersey, would constitute an indictable offense) for eight years following the release from post-conviction custody or from the date of sentencing if the person was not incarcerated; Disorderly persons convictions or municipal ordinance violations in New Jersey (or, if from any other state or jurisdiction, convictions for conduct which, if committed in New Jersey, would constitute a disorderly persons offense or municipal ordinance violation) for five years following the release from post-conviction custody or from the date of sentencing if the person was not incarcerated
rules.summary: Landlords may only consider indictable offense convictions from the past 8 years and disorderly persons or municipal violations from the past 5 years, with certain serious crimes (murder, arson, sex offenses requiring registry, terrorism) considered regardless of when they occurred, and may not consider arrests without convictions, expunged records, or juvenile records.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to rental, lease, or sublease of real property, except single apartments in two-family dwellings where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in owner-occupied single-family dwellings.
rules.exemption_note: Exemptions for owner-occupied two-family dwellings (one unit rented) and rooms in owner-occupied single-family dwellings.
rules.penalty: First violation: fine up to $500. Each subsequent violation: fine up to $1,000.

rules.title: Ban the Box for Housing - Required Considerations and Individualized Assessment
rules.quote: A landlord or real estate broker shall consider the following factors in evaluating the applicant and the results of any criminal history inquiry, conducted in accordance with the limitations of Section 2:31-3: Any information, if provided, pertaining to the degree of rehabilitation and good conduct or to the accuracy of the criminal record in question produced by the applicant, or produced on his or her behalf to the landlord or real estate broker, including but not limited to any certificate of rehabilitation issued by any state or federal agency, which includes but is not limited to certificates issued pursuant to N.J.S.A. 2A:168A-1 to 16; The amount of time that has passed since the conviction(s) and/or release from custody; and The nature of and circumstances surrounding the crime(s).
rules.summary: When evaluating criminal history, landlords and real estate brokers must consider evidence of rehabilitation and good conduct, the time elapsed since the conviction or release, and the nature and circumstances of the crime.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to rental, lease, or sublease of real property, except single apartments in two-family dwellings where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in owner-occupied single-family dwellings.
rules.exemption_note: Exemptions for owner-occupied two-family dwellings (one unit rented) and rooms in owner-occupied single-family dwellings.
rules.penalty: First violation: fine up to $500. Each subsequent violation: fine up to $1,000.

rules.title: Ban the Box for Housing - Advertisement Restrictions
rules.quote: In connection with any rental, lease, or sublease, it shall be unlawful for a landlord or real estate broker to produce or disseminate any advertisement that directly or indirectly references the use or consideration of an applicant's criminal history, except that nothing in this section shall preclude the expression of statutory, regulatory, or rule-based eligibility restrictions applicable to the rental, lease or sublease of real property as described in Section 2:31-8a so long as such expression is limited to the specified offense(s) and time period(s) as established by law.
rules.summary: Landlords and real estate brokers may not advertise that they will consider applicants' criminal history, except for specific statutory restrictions.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to rental, lease, or sublease of real property, except single apartments in two-family dwellings where owner occupies the other unit, or rooms in owner-occupied single-family dwellings.
rules.exemption_note: Exemptions for owner-occupied two-family dwellings (one unit rented) and rooms in owner-occupied single-family dwellings.
rules.penalty: First violation: fine up to $500. Each subsequent violation: fine up to $1,000.
